chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, who said:

I sent a message to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'I have young children, so when does zakat become obligatory upon their wealth?' He said: 'When prayer becomes obligatory upon them, zakat becomes obligatory upon them.' I said: 'And what about those upon whom prayer has not yet become obligatory?' He said: 'When they are traded with (i.e., their wealth is used in commerce), then pay their zakat.'
ai.seo_question: When does zakat become obligatory on the wealth of young children in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Sahih al-Tusi clarifies that the obligation of zakat on children's wealth is tied to the capacity for commercial activity rather than mere puberty, distinguishing it from the ritual obligation of prayer. Scholars note this establishes a practical standard where wealth is subject to zakat once it is actively engaged in trade, ensuring the purification of assets even for those not yet fully liable for all religious duties.
